audit.whatIsWrong: Five chart rows disagree with the packet, and the packet defect flags the chart as contradicting the data outright.
audit.why: Level 1 is genuinely yours — the page's own whys[0] says Jax has nothing online — yet the row reads Skill. Levels 4-5 and 6 read Skill under text that calls them 'Jax's window and he knows it'. The packet reads Swain, Skill, Jax, Jax, Jax, Jax, Skill and the mirror set exactly that with ratings 3, 5, 7, 7, 7, 7, 5 on its side, which inverts to 7, 5, 3, 3, 3, 3, 5 here.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 4, 5 and 7 flipped in matched pairs, with all seven ratings set to the inverse of the mirror's.

audit.why: Spike timings hold — your level 1, his level 3, his 6-plus, his two items — but spikes[2] misdescribed what his ultimate actually gives him.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grandmaster-at-Arms is described in three places as a 'passive resistance' that 'stacks during fights'.
audit.why: Riot's text splits it: the passive is bonus magic damage on every third consecutive attack; the armour and magic resist come from ACTIVATING it, and only for a short duration. That difference decides the advice — a stacking passive would mean never fighting him long, while a short activated buff means the correct play is to wait the few seconds out and then drain.
audit.corrected: Passive and active separated, with the resist window described as brief and waitable.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[1] gives Counter Strike an 8-second cooldown.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9 seconds. Eight is Leap Strike's number at rank 1, and the error makes his defensive window look twice as available as it is — at level 2 you actually have a 17-second gap to work in.
audit.corrected: 17 seconds at rank 1 written in, with the trade advice keyed to it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Empower is never named as an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: It is a 3-second-cooldown charge that empowers his next attack — the wind-up, not the cast, is the moment to step out.

edits.before: Counter Strike is level 2 now but its 8-second cooldown creates windows — poke when it is down, root his Q-leap when he tries to close.
edits.after: Counter Strike arrives at 2 but costs him 17 seconds at rank 1 — that gap is the window: poke while it is down and root his Leap Strike.

edits.before: Jax's R passive resistance stacks during fights, directly countering Demonic Ascension's drain by reducing the magic damage you heal from — extended fights now favor him.
edits.after: Grandmaster-at-Arms only grants armour and magic resist when he activates it, and briefly — so your drain does least in that short window; wait it out instead of extending.

edits.before: Jax's R passive stacks between his E cycles and his item spikes compound fast — he controls fights from here through two items.
edits.after: His ultimate adds magic damage on every third strike, with a resist boost on activation, and items compound it — he controls fights through two items.

edits.before: Stack his passive resistance with R active during your Demonic Ascension to outlast your healing window
edits.after: Time Grandmaster-at-Arms so its armour and magic resist are up exactly when your drain starts

edits.before: Levels 4 through 6 are Jax's window and he knows it. His Counter Strike cooldown drops and he will pattern into: Q-leap whenever your E is down, Counter Strike immediately to null your W auto-attack, stun, then land the full W-burst. Your job is to stay near max W range, poke the wave, and only fish for E-root when he walks up without Q available. At level 6 his R passive resistance gives him physical and magic damage reduction stacking in a fight — if he activates R during your Demonic Ascension drain you will lose the attrition war. Avoid extended fights here; poke, root, extract value, and back off.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 6 are Jax's window and he knows it. Counter Strike falls from 17 seconds toward 9 and he patterns into it: Leap Strike whenever your E is down, Counter Strike to eat your autos, stun, then the Empower hit. Empower is a reset with a visible charge — that wind-up is your cue to step out, not the moment he casts. Stay at max W range, poke the wave, and fish the root only when he walks up with Leap Strike spent. At 6 the resists come from activating his ultimate and last only a few seconds, so do not open your drain into it — let the buff lapse, then commit. Poke, root, take value, leave.

notes: Grandmaster-at-Arms was described three times as a passive that stacks resistances during a fight. It is not: the passive is bonus magic damage on every third consecutive attack, and the armour and magic resist come from activating it for a short duration. That flips the instruction from 'never fight him long' to 'let the buff lapse, then drain', which is the actually winnable line. Counter Strike's cooldown was given as 8 seconds — that is Leap Strike; Counter Strike is 17 at rank 1 falling to 9, so the level 2 window is far larger than the page suggested. Five chart rows flipped in matched pairs with all seven ratings set to the inverse of the mirror's, since the packet defect explicitly flagged a chart giving Jax four stages to Swain's one against a 52.2% win rate.
